s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic abdominal pain and altered bowel habits with significant weight loss
salient_findings: Recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, bloating, and obstipation
key_facts: Colonoscopy and esophagogastroduodenoscopy showed no abnormalities
Exploratory laparotomy showed no mechanical cause of the obstructions
Alcohol use stopped 2 years ago due to worsening symptoms
Gluten-free diet trialed for 3 months produced no improvement

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic abdominal pain and altered bowel habits with significant weight loss
salient_findings: Recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, bloating, and obstipation
key_facts: Colonoscopy and esophagogastroduodenoscopy showed no abnormalities
Exploratory laparotomy showed no mechanical cause of the obstructions
Alcohol use stopped 2 years ago due to worsening symptoms
Gluten-free diet trialed for 3 months produced no improvement

shortlist.label: Chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, bloating, and obstipation, with no mechanical cause found on exploratory laparotomy

shortlist.label: Intestinal lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Significant weight loss and low levels of fat-soluble vitamins, which could indicate malabsorption or malignancy

shortlist.label: Celiac disease
shortlist.why_kept: Despite initial colonoscopy and esophagogastroduodenoscopy showing no evidence, gluten-free diet trial was attempted, but patient's symptoms could still be related to celiac disease or other malabsorptive conditions

shortlist.label: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth
shortlist.why_kept: History of abdominal symptoms, bloating, and diarrhea, which could be related to bacterial overgrowth

shortlist.label: Intestinal amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Low levels of fat-soluble vitamins and significant weight loss, which could indicate amyloidosis or other infiltrative diseases

raw.rationale: The patient's 20-year history of recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, bloating, and obstipation, alternating with intermittent diarrhea, and the absence of any mechanical cause of obstruction on exploratory laparotomy, along with the presence of small-bowel dilation and megacolon, are consistent with chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction.

rejected.label: Intestinal lymphoma
rejected.why: There is no mention of a mass or tumor on imaging or endoscopy.

rejected.label: Celiac disease
rejected.why: Colonoscopy and esophagogastroduodenoscopy showed no evidence of celiac disease, and a gluten-free diet trialed for 3 months produced no improvement.

rejected.label: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth
rejected.why: While possible, the patient's symptoms and findings are more consistent with a motility disorder than an infectious or inflammatory process.

rejected.label: Intestinal amyloidosis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence of amyloidosis, such as proteinuria or characteristic histopathological findings, to support this diagnosis.
